Is this you?

You care where every cent went.

UnPAIN is not trying to be for everyone. It's built for one very specific kind of person.

  • You care where every cent went
  • You actually open the "Statistics" page
  • You compare spending month over month
  • …and year over year
  • You keep many categories and defend each one
  • You have a folder of receipts "just in case"
  • You like dashboards a suspicious amount
  • You promised yourself "next month I'll stop using Excel"

Especially good for couples who want a genuinely fair way to split expenses — proportional to income, not a lazy 50/50. And if you live in Germany, it quietly sorts your tax-relevant spending all year long.

If none of that sounds like you, that's fine. This probably isn't your tool — and we're at peace with that.

Why another finance app?

Because I tried almost all of them.

Some had beautiful mobile apps.

Some automatically synchronized my bank.

Some had great reports.

Every single one eventually sent me back to Excel.

Not because they were bad.

Because they weren't built for someone like me.

So I stopped looking —

and built UnPAIN.

What makes it different

Precision without the chaos.

Automation that respects your obsession

We don't remove the detail. We remove the repetition. You'll never categorize the same supermarket 300 times — teach a merchant once, and it remembers forever.

Your data never leaves your machine

No cloud. No telemetry. No subscription. No login. You own your financial history — today and in ten years.

Fair, not equal

Shared costs split in proportion to income. When two people earn differently, 50/50 isn't fair. It just looks tidy.

A German tax bonus

Not the main product — a gift for people in Germany. Refund-relevant spending, sorted into the right buckets all year, ready for ELSTER or a Steuerberater.

Open source, on purpose

Not a licence footnote. Owning your financial data forever is the whole philosophy. The code is yours to read, run, and keep.

Deterministic core

Parsing, rules, currency, settlement and tax are plain, auditable math — recomputed from your data, never guessed, never stored derived.

How it works

Drop. Review. Done.

Three steps a month. After a few months, step two nearly disappears.

Drop your exports

Download the CSV from each bank and drop the files in one folder. PDF-only statements go through deterministic extractors.

Review the queue

Work through a short queue in the browser. "Apply + rule" teaches the system permanently, so it categorizes itself next time.

Close the month

Check the dashboard, then close the month. Every year carries your rules and categories forward automatically.

Fair, not equal

Equal is not always fair.

When two people earn differently, splitting shared costs 50/50 quietly makes the lower earner pay a bigger share of their income. UnPAIN splits in proportion to income instead — a monthly estimate, and a binding true-up after the year closes.

Alex — earns 60%pays 60%
Sam — earns 40%pays 40%

Only salary counts toward the ratio. One transfer settles the difference.

The manifesto
  • We believe details matter.
  • We believe your data belongs to you.
  • We believe automation should remove work, not control.
  • We believe fairness isn't always 50/50.
  • We believe spreadsheets deserve a peaceful retirement.
The final page of this conversation

Hi, I'm Leandro 👋

I'm a software engineer living in Germany.

I didn't build UnPAIN because I wanted to build a finance app. I built it because I was tired of maintaining a spreadsheet every single month.

For years, I ran my household finances on increasingly elaborate Excel sheets. Eventually one of them got more complicated than the software I write for a living — so I gave it a proper home.

It's open source because I suspect I'm not the only person who enjoys knowing exactly where every cent went. If that sounds familiar… welcome home.
